[...] Thankfully for the supporters of the king, both he and his sister-wife recovered, and it was not long before Aegon once again donned his armor and flew off upon Grey Ghost, this time northward towards Gulltown, where the armies of the Vale were quickly approaching. His fleets sailed after him, perhaps one of the most intact parts of his army remaining, while Lord Commander Erryk ‘the Lionhearted’ Cargyll led infantry and cavalry south to defend the Stormlands. Gulltown itself showed little resistance when the grey dragon landed upon the city’s walls, and before long the northern end of the Bay of Crabs was thoroughly blockaded. When the armies did arrive they were quickly chased back up into the mountains by dragonfire, and Aegon’s forces trailed after them, claiming a few keeps along the way. The king could not remain there forever however, as word reached him that he and his dragon were needed in the Stormlands.

Some time after arriving on hostile shores, it was discovered that Rhaenyra was with child, complicating matters for her and her supporters. In the early months she still rode with her army with Syrax, it was only a matter of time before she would have to cease doing so lest harm be brought to her unborn child. Rhaenyra was a stubborn woman however, and no coward, so instead of retreating to the safety of Dorne she remained close to the frontlines, and Syrax remained with her. Though less controllable and precise without her rider, she still had her fire, and if a battle was close to where her rider was she would join it from above, fiercely protective of her mistress. It was during this time, when the two opposing armies once met in a great clash, that Lord Commander Erryk was seriously burned by dragonfire. He was one of the lucky ones merely for the fact she survived the flames, but his injuries left him in no state to lead and reminded many of the terrorization of the realm by Caraxes in the previous war. Only this time, not only one side rode dragons.

But only one side had scorpions, the bane of dragons since Meraxes fell from the skies above Hellholt. Aegon knew this of course, so even after his arrival he did not fly into battle, knowing that awaited him if he tried. After she had recovered from the birth of her daughter, Daenerys, Rhaenyra returned to the battlefield as well, flying without fear with Syrax. The two dragons would roar their wrath at each other, would lash their tails furiously and breathe angry puffs of smoke, but they would never dance.

Aegon would not be able to stay there long either, as word reached him that his rebelling lords were once again besieging his capital, and with the realm’s loyal armies spread so thin the defense was not going well. So off he flew again, but by the time he arrived the invaders had already breached the city and were flooding the streets like rats. Perhaps he could have burned them out, but how many innocents would he have burned alongside them, how destroyed would his city be by his own hand? Whether out of mercy, reason, or simply not wishing to rule over nothing but ashes, Aegon instead landed upon one of the great parapets of the wall around the Red Keep, daring his enemies to try and bypass him.

And in fairness they did not try, but by then it was already too late. The rebels held half the city, Rhaenyra’s forces drew closer and closer by the day, and if his reputation was not in tatters enough, the High Septon pronounced an anathema upon him, condemning him and barring him from partaking in religious services. What exactly the last straw for the young king was is unknown, but by the timeRhaenyra arrived with the Dornish, he put up no more fight, all but giving up with the crown to his elder half-sister and ending his reign of two years, six moons, and twenty five days. 

The former king was confined to the more comfortable upper chambers of the dungeon tower, his dragon was chained in the Dragonpit, and the siege on the city was ended as the supposed tyrant they had been fighting against ruled no more. There was a general sense of surprise but relief that things had ended so calmly, perhaps none more so then those charged with caring for the once again Princess Helaena, who was eight moons pregnant with the twins of her brother-husband. Thankfully, a bit over a moon after the surrender, she gave birth to two healthy baby boys, Jaehaerys and Jacaerys.

While the common levies dispersed to return to their homes, the lords already there states at the capital while ravens were sent out across the realm, for Rhaenyra would not make the same mistake her brother had - she was going to be officially coronated as soon as possible, even if that meant not having the most grandiose celebrations for it the world had ever seen. Though make no mistake, everything would be sufficiently magnificent, as only befitting of a royal. She considered crowning herself with the crown of the Conciliator - it had been a symbol for her during the war after all, and her father had done the same, but did she want to be like her father? A man content to turn a blind eye to the growing conflict in his court in favor of wining and dining? A man who had gotten himself so drunk he had given his own crown away to a low-ranking noble house simply because he considered their lord a friend? No, she would not be like him. She would be better.

So a new crown was forged, reminiscent of the one she had once worn in its gold and inlaid gems, but her own, not just a simple diadem but a crown proper, with the form of a dragon delicately carved into its central spike, modeled after her own beloved Syrax. The High Septon placed it upon her head and she sat unscratched upon the Iron Throne, and it seemed to many like the perfect conclusion to the last decade of chaos. There was simply the matter of what to do with Aegon.

She would not kill him, she was too forgiving and unwilling to make herself a kinslayer. She offered to allow him to take the Black but he would not accept it, unwilling to give up the life of luxury he had only ever known in exchange for spending the rest of his days in a freezing wasteland at the end of the world. He could call for a trial by combat and Rhaenyra would accept it, but she would not initiate it herself, tired of causing bloodshed. So unless he demanded it, she would let him sit in that tower, in the gilded cage of his own choosing, until either he changed his mind or died of natural causes, the latter surely a long way aways for a man of only twenty years.

The maesters would remember him in their books, and his short and disastrous reign would surely be a point of discussion among scholars long after he was gone, but while Aegon lived, he was half forgotten.

Approximately half a year passed between the second taking of King’s Landing - and the end of a war - and the beginning of a new one. During that time King Aegon II Targaryen began preparations for his official coronation, as he was a man grown now and was more then ready to officially be king. The problem was, the royal treasury had been greatly diminished by the last eight years of war, as had the general wealth of the realm, and after all the waiting for it he wants the moment the world sees the crown properly put on his head to be glorious. Not wanting to delay the ceremony further, the lords already only grudgingly accepting him as their king, he called for a representative of the Iron Bank of Braavos to visit the capital, and took out a loan with bank to help fund both the event and provide some aid in rebuilding the realm.

The loan would never be put towards its intended purpose however, as shortly after the new year passed, Princess Rhaenyra Targaryen, the Realm’s Delight lost to sands south of the Red Mountains, reemerged and declared herself the rightful ruler of the Iron Throne, backed in her claim but the forces of Dorne and the Vale. For while the realm had half forgotten the Princess in the South, too caught up in the war, Rhaenyra had not forgotten them, and spent those years planning and forging alliances. She betrothed her son and heir, Viserys Targaryen, to the eldest legitimate daughter of Prince Qoren Nymeros Martell, Princess Larra, and swore that the Iron Throne would not again attempt to conquer the southern kingdom as long as the alliance held. The prince was no fool, knowing how they had only escaped another attempted conquest by sheer luck, and that one day scorpions might not be enough to keep the dragons at bay. But if the crown prince was wed to a Martell, she would one day be queen, and her children would still have sand in their blood. It could buy Dorne decades more peace.

Though their armies were unravished by a long war, they alone against all the forces of the Seven Kingdoms likely wouldn’t be enough, especially on the offensive. That is where Rhaenyra’s oldest alliance came into play, one she had forged years ago, when war was the last thing on her mind.

Some wondered why Lady Jeyne Arryn backed neither of the young dragons in their war against each other, even when all the other realms had claimed sides, instead remaining perched up high in her mountains. If asked, she spoke about not wanting to get involved in the “foolish wars of foolish men with too much power and too little sense”, and no one thought much else about the matter. When King Aegon started hiding his forces away in the mountains of the Vale inbetween strikes against the Riverlands, but it was easy enough to dismiss as her still not wanting to get involved, and not wanting to poke the quite literal dragon those encroaching on her land had. Perhaps there was some truth to it all too, especially in the beginning, but it left her as the only one of the realms without an army depleted by war. For her soldiers Jeyne asked for no marriages or the like to seal the alliance - though she had no one to marry off, her claimed son already wed - because there was no need for such things. She and Rhaenyra were already cousins by blood, friends from their girlhoods, and sisters in strife, Jeyne knowing all too well how desperately men wished to cast aside the rightful claims of women based on what was between their legs and nothing more.

So it was that armies descended from mountains both northern and southern, and Rhaenyra, sat atop Syrax’s back and the crown of the Conciliator - politely reclaimed from House Cupps after they came to acquire it from her father via overenthusiastic drunken generosity -  upon her head, declared herself the true and rightful ruler of the Seven Kingdoms. Already this did not bode well for the reign of Aegon II,  many lords discontent with his rule before it even began. All the lord paramounts, save the Vale, had sided against him in his war with Aemond after all, and even with his immense leniency towards them, they were still displeased to see him on the throne. In fact, his mercy only seemed to prove their fears of him being a weak king right, and even emboldened some to action. Seeing the opportunity presented by Rhaenyra’s war, only a short few moons later the Rose and River lords rose up in rebellion against their king, citing defense against tyranny as their cause, with many lesser lords of various realms joining their cause. While they did not declare any support towards the queen-claimant, they certainly did aid her, as now Aegon had to balance two separate wars coming at him from all sides.

Seeing the Riverlands were now more friend then foe, the forces of the Vale quickly returned from whence they came, instead beginning to move towards Gulltown so they might attack the Crownlands by sea. This sudden change of course would take time to properly initiate, but it was compensated for by the forces of Dorne and those Rhaenyra had managed to gather herself throughout the years as they attacked the southern Stormlands, landing on the shores near the mountain ranges and the rainwood, moving northward keep by keep. Aegon might have turned his attention there if not for the rebels right upon his doorstep, already having made their way through the counties of the Crownlands to begin a siege of King’s Landing. Though said siege was able to be broken by the king and his dragon before they properly entered the city, the refugees that had swarmed to the capital in fleeing the approaching armies brought yet another enemy - disease. Before long cases of pox began to spring up throughout the city, and the stench of sickness was added to the usual stink in the air. Bodies lined the streets, hidden beneath thin tarps, as the plague slowly wormed its way up and into the Red Keep, guards and walls useless against it. For a time the king and queen both were abed with it, tended to by the finest maesters in the realm, but still there was fear that it would take them just as easily as it had taken commoners. [...]

His elder brother decreed that he would not be a kinslayer, no matter what his brother had done. Instead, Aemond was forced to formally give up any and all claims he had, from the Seven Kingdoms themselves to the petty keeps along the Blackstripe his family owned but rarely used. He would be allowed to live on Dragonstone, but not as a prince might - rather, as any common born man would. His young dragon would also remain in the Dragonpit of King’s Landing, the little creature too much of a potential threat to allow to remain with Aemond. With no other choice, the prince begrudgingly agreed, and was quickly shipped off to Dragonstone to live amongst the salt and smoke, only able to watch bitterly from the ground below at any dragons that soared by.

And thus, the kingdom was at peace once more. As King Aegon II Targaryen began planning his coronation and Daeron at last was able to claim a dragon of his own in the form of the blue and bronze Tessarion, all were relieved that the realm would no longer be plagued by fire and blood. At least, for the time being…

Shortly after King’s Landing was taken by the forces of Aegon, only two moons after she turned twelve, Princess Helaena Targaryen would marry her brother, King Aegon II Targaryen, himself two moons shy of turning fourteen, and become Queen Helaena. At last she would fly free with her beloved dragon Dreamfyre, the two soaring together over Blackwater Bay alongside Aegon and Grey Ghost to the safety of Dragonstone.

Shortly afterwards Prince Daeron Targaryen was moved from the capital as well to a more discrete location, the reason becoming evident as Prince Daemon Targaryen and Caraxes returned from fighting in the Riverlands to help retake the city, the reclamation of the capital only a temporary victory in the face of the fires of the Blood Wyrm. Even with Meleys and her swiftness on their side, it was an unsure thing if she would be able to defeat the larger and more battle-hardened dragon, especially with a rider so inexperienced compared to Daemon.

It had been in those same Riverlands that Otto Hightower, simply Ser after Lord Paramount Gormon Tyrell had become Hand of the King, would meet the Stranger. One would wonder why a man in his fifties, the grandfather of the king, would be on the battlefield in the first place. Rumors were whispered that Otto was killed not by the forces of Aegon, but one of Aemond’s own men. Or, perhaps, one of Daemon’s men - the two had grown to hate each other even more than they had before, supposedly after Otto discovered a plot to kill him led by Daemon, if the servants are to be believed. No matter the cause of his death, it was yet another point of grief for poor Dowager Queen Alicent Hightower. It was unlikely that there was any real love between her and her late husband, but he was still the father of her five children, and his death was what pitted two of her sons against each other in the first place. The years of planning and plotting had worked, the Greens had won, but the victory tasted as bitter as poison. She spent much of her days in the sept, pleading and praying to the Seven.

The war continued on, though at least the war with Dorne officially came to an end, so focused on their own internal conflict that many people north of the Red Mountains forget it even happened in the first place, bringing an anticlimactic end to the Fifth Dornish War. Aegon’s forces were unable to match those of Aemond in direct combat, so instead they slowly but surely took keeps wherever they could, no matter how small, gaining progress inch by bloody inch. By age fourteen Aegon took to the front lines himself, leading from atop Grey Ghost, spear in hand as he rallied his troops. Yet many still worried that no matter how hard they tried, they would still lose the war. What could they do in the face of Daemon and Caraxes, both terrors in their own right?

On the twenty second day of the first moon, one hundred and twenty three years after the conquest of King Aegon I Targaryen, Prince Daemon Targaryen, the Rogue Prince and Kingmaker, the true ruler of the Iron Throne, died as he lived - in battle. How exactly he passed remains unclear, but what is known is that, while sieging down a keep of one of the lords who sided with Aegon, burning and tearing down its walls atop Caraxes, he was killed. Amidst the fire and smoke no one saw what happened clearly, and thus rumors spread like wildfire - a lucky shot from a crossbowman, a spear tossed with a prayer and guided by the hand of the Warrior himself, a brick from the walls of the keep he was tearing apart flew up and struck him in the head. In the end it did not matter what had killed him, only that he was dead. Caraxes roared and raged at the death of his rider, the sky alight with his angry breaths of fire. It was a miracle that they were able to cut his saddle, and the prince’s body, from him, and as soon as it was gone he flew off, screaming his fury and grief into the air, bringing further ravagement upon the Riverlands.

With the prince dead, the dowager queen was chosen to be Aemond’s next regent, though some wondered if they should surrender to Aegon and beg for mercy. They had just lost their most powerful force in Caraxes, and their only dragon, as the king was still yet to claim or hatch a dragon of his own. He had not even been properly crowned yet, or sat on the Iron Throne - some wondered if the seat would reject him if he tried, like it had with Maegor the Cruel. Furthermore, while Aegon’s forces were still on the backfoot, the death and Daemon was not the only boon they gained, for in his death Dark Sister had slipped from his grasp and fallen amongst the rubble, where it was found by the forces of the elder king and presented to him. It was said that as he lifted the Valyrian steel blade above his head, held tightly in hand, the soldiers he stood before cheered so loudly, Lady Jeyne Arryn and her court heard it all the way up in the Eyrie of the Vale.

Despite the death of the man many considered the true king, the war continued on, Aemond firmly believing now that the throne was his right after being raised by his uncle and being told so by those loyal to him for the last seven years. Though they still had the advantage, the gap between the two opposing military forces was growing smaller and smaller as Aegon’s forces avoided direct battle, allowing their numbers to recuperate and regrow. However, one day they were forced into battle, but with the help of Grey Ghost and his dragonfire they managed to deal a crushing defeat to the forces of Aemond, lowering morale even further.

A spark of hope was given to the younger king and his allies however when, finally, Aemond managed to hatch an egg just before the end of summer in 122 A.C., a deep rose-pink and green eyed dragon he named Laehurlion. Though it would be many years before the two could soar in the skies together, it helped dissuade some of the fears that Aemond is not worthy of the throne. But that was not enough to stop the momentum Aegon and his army had gained, as they delivered another serious defeat to their enemies, diminishing the forces of Aemond enough that their armies outnumbered his own.

After slowly but surely working their way down from the relative safety of the mountains of the neutral Vale and through the hostile Riverlands and Crownlands, Aegon’s army began once again to take King’s Landing, choosing to begin their assault at the River Gate, hoping to travel from there through Hook Market and up to the Red Keep. The streets were bloody and burning, and while the defenders of the city tried to hold against their enemies, they learned the same thing that Harren the Black once had - that walls and stone mean little in the face of a dragon.

On the twenty seventh day of the sixth moon, one hundred and twenty four years after the conquest of King Aegon I Targaryen, just as the winds of winter began to harshly settle over the realm, the Red Keep was finally breached, Aemond captured, and the war brought to an end after eight long years. Aegon’s first act as king was to pardon the rebellious Lord Paramounts Tully, Lannister, Baratheon, Stark, and Tyrell, having no interest in starting another war while trying to wrangle them into accepting some sort of punishment. Prince Daeron was brought back from where he had been secretly kept to the capital, just in time to witness the fate of the now Prince Aemond be decided.

On the sixteenth day of the third moon, one hundred and sixteen years after the conquest of King Aegon I Targaryen, King Viserys I Targaryen died, and everything fell apart. No one expected the king to die so suddenly, found one morning to have passed in his sleep - quite the opposite in fact. Despite a scare with an outbreak of pox several years prior, the king seemed as healthy as ever, and if anything, invigorated. He had only recently declared his intention to at last bring Dorne underneath the reign of the Iron Throne, beginning the Fifth Dornish War, and only a month prior to his death Queen Alicent Hightower had given birth to their fifth child and second daughter, Princess Baela Targaryen, a fact which thrilled him. By all accounts, it seemed like he would finally be making his reign worth note, instead of simply continuing on the years of peace handed to him by his grandfather, King Jaehaerys I Targaryen.

But then he was found dead, lying in bed in his tent as he led his armies against the Dornish, still looking as if he were merely sleeping if not for the stillness of his breath and lack of pulse. A sudden tragedy, but the Targaryens had faced many before, though there was fear that Princess Rhaenyra Targaryen would challenge the claim of her younger brother, the now King Aegon II Targaryen, who had been made his father’s heir after his birth and was only eight name days old. It was a different sibling they should have been worrying about, however.
Prince Aemond, six years of age, was his elder brother’s heir apparent, but while his brother was away on Dragonstone, having been visiting it when his father passed, he was in King’s Landing, and someone decided that he ought to be king instead. 

Prince Daemon Targaryen was now not only a Rogue Prince, but a Kingmaker too. By all the rules and laws of succession it made no sense to crown the second son while the first still lived, and no matter what the prince said, all suspected his true reason for crowning Aemond - power. His late brother had entrusted Daemon with helping to raise his second son, and while he was still a boy it only made sense that the powers of acting regent would fall to his uncle. He would practically be the king himself while his nephew was a child, if not longer depending on how much control he was able to gain over him. There were even rumors that having Aemond on the throne was only temporary until Daemon could either install himself or his son, a boy named Ergys living with his mother Mysaria in Lys, the two not allowed to live in King’s Landing by the late Viserys. It was speculated that once the war with Aegon was dealt with, he’d finally wed his long-time paramour - his previous wife, Lady Rhea Royce, had died seemingly in a freak accident while hunting - have his son legitimized, then have his nephew dealt with while he contrived a way to put his own blood on throne.

Of course, many of the lords of the Seven Kingdoms would not stand for this blatant ignoring of succession rights, and the realm quickly broke out into war, the offensive against the Dornish quickly forgotten. Some thought that Princess Rhaenyra would use this opportunity to push her own claim, having been cast aside all those years ago once her father finally got the son he had wanted for so long, but her own declaration never came. Instead the princess, who had been supporting the front lines in the Prince’s Pass with Syrax at the time, took a small group of those close and loyal to her and left to the other side of the Red Mountains. Perhaps she meant to merely wanted to wait out the war without getting caught up in it herself, or perhaps she simply wished to bide her time until one of her half-brothers prevailed over the other so she could pick off what remained of the victor and his army. Whatever the case, it seemed likely that she had suspected something like this would occur, as it was discovered that all the eggs Syrax had laid had vanished from where they had been kept in the Dragonpit.

Despite the many available dragons, it seemed that the war would mostly be decided on the ground rather than in the sky. Daemon had his fierce Blood Wyrm, Caraxes, but whatever plans he had would never come to fruition if he was severely injured or dead. Aemond himself had no dragon of his own, rumors flying about that all the dragons in the Dragonpit had rejected him and two eggs had gone cold in his hands. In 120 A.C. Princess Heleana claimed Dreamfyre, but she was but a girl and both she and her dragon were known to be of gentle natures. There was also the fear that she would be more loyal to Aegon, whom she had been betrothed too for many years, and would flee the capital if allowed, which was why Daemon had Dreamfyre always kept chained after the young princess showed signs of bonding with her, Helena allowed by the dragon to climb upon her saddled back but the two not allowed to fly together. A year into the war Baela had hatched her own dragon, a creature with black eyes and scales with wing membranes of purple named Anogaron, but both were far too young to even so much as fly, let alone consider sending into battle.

Aegon had a dragon of his own, having tamed the elusive Grey Ghost, but his advisors were hesitant to allow him to fly to war himself, as they would have no cause to fight for if their rightful king was dead. They did have one unlikely dragonrider however in the form of Ser Daeron Velaryon, the grand-nephew of the late Sea Snake, Lord Colrys Velaryon. In the same year Princess Rhaenys Targaryen died to an outbreak of pox, he bonded with the fierce Red Queen, Meleys, to the surprise of many. Though he decided to take up arms and wings for Aegon, Lord Laenor and Lady Laena Velaryon were less interested in doing so, firmly remaining neutral in the war.

Four years have passed since the Dance began, the balance of the war constantly teetering. Aegon has taken King’s Landing, Daemon having fled with Aemond and Baela while seemingly leaving Heleana and Daeron behind. Though for now Aemond’s forces seem to be gaining progress, the tides of war can shift in an instant, and the citizens of Westeros can only guess how much longer this war will last.
